cells.tense: You are being tested by what you have already set in motion, and you stay with it while the test runs.
cells.ask: Name one next step in this that is small enough to finish today, and do that one.
cells.core:
You are in a stretch where only the next step is lit. You know that, and you are still walking it. What you have committed to is being tested by friction, not by argument, and you are not flinching from the test. Not certainty — just enough light for the next step and the willingness to take it.

The care here is not exhausting you. You let growth happen without forcing it, and because of that the thing you are committed to has room to grow. The next thing you feed gets to be this, not a new worry. Same direction, same quiet patience.
cells.sheetLine: Enough light for the next step, and you keep taking it.
cells.verb: to keep testing a commitment by handing it into real friction
cells.place: in the half-lit middle stretch, moving by the next step you can actually see

cells.tense: You are running the test ahead of time in your head, bracing for a friction that has not arrived yet.
cells.ask: Take one thing you are rehearsing in your head and put it down for today.
cells.core:
You are trying to finish the test before it is over. Somewhere ahead there is a version where the friction is resolved and the commitment is proven, and you are living in that version now, rehearsing the outcome, checking the plan for holes before the day has asked anything of you. The bracing eats the thing you are bracing for.

When this runs too hot, it reaches for direction in a way that crowds out the actual next step. The fix is not to care less. It is to let one act of care stay a real act, in real time, without a preview running underneath it. The friction will come when it comes.

cells.tense: You stopped testing the commitment some time back, and you still stand at the door as if the choice were ahead of you.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you are actually committed to, and stop there.
cells.core:
You have gone quiet on the testing. Not because the commitment is gone — it still holds you — but because you stopped bringing it into contact with anything that could show you where it stands. The door is behind you, and you are still waiting for it to open.

What is missing is not more certainty. It is one small act of contact, the kind that asks something of the commitment and lets you hear the answer. You do not have to feel ready first. Let one person in on one thing you are holding, without asking them to carry it.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you and you are still waiting at it.

cells.tense: You are already testing the commitment in what you do day to day, and you speak of it as if nothing were being decided.
cells.ask: Name one choice from today that was really a decision about this, and say it was yours.
cells.core:
You are already testing this. It shows in what you choose to keep doing when it would be easier to stop, in the small adjustments you make without announcing them, in the way you return to the same effort after a bad day. That is engagement, and it is doing real work. But you describe it as just how things happen to be going.

You are the one holding this commitment in place, and when it gets talked about as though it were simply there, you lose the credit and the choice. The simplest version of what you are building is still yours. Say so, once, and watch what that does.
cells.sheetLine: You are already testing it. You just have not said so.

attempts.check: The pull is that Dedication is being spent on something and the person can feel it — the record gives the card and the status, not the object or whether the commitment is wise, so no cell may name what they are devoted to or rate it. If the reader says the test is not a private one but a public deadline, the asks still stand because each is a small visible act in the seat's own register, not a verdict on the commitment. The line that serves me as writer is the 'private contest' framing dressed as fact; the cells keep it to what a person would notice behind closed doors and leave the history blank.
